To explain how a local inference engine balances GPU memory, host memory, and token latency, we must look at the architectural constraints of Large Language Model (LLM) inference. The core challenge is the **Memory-Compute Trade-off**: LLMs are memory-bound, not compute-bound. The bottleneck is usually moving data (weights and KV cache) from storage to the compute unit (GPU), not the arithmetic itself.

Here is a detailed technical breakdown of how modern local inference engines (e.g., llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM) balance these three factors.

To explain how a local inference engine balances GPU memory, host memory, and token latency, we must look at the architectural constraints of Large Language Model (LLM) inference. The core challenge is that **GPU memory is fast but limited**, while **host (CPU/RAM) memory is slow but abundant**. Token latency is the output metric that suffers when data moves between these two domains.

Below is a detailed technical breakdown of the mechanisms used to balance these three factors.
